architecture_decision: hot path is 100% CPU-bound (AVX2 only); GPU/CAGRA reserved exclusively for background batch refit (Section 4.4) and Control Plane (Dataiku) historical batch search

fused_hot_path_measurement.description: Layer 1 (commutator) + Layer 2 (centroid lookup, K=100) measured as a single fused function call per tick, not summed from separate measurements

component_breakdown_measured_separately.note: fused measurement (1.81us) is lower than the sum of separate means (2.10us), consistent with shared warmup and cache-locality benefits when both operations run back-to-back in one measured call rather than as two independent benchmark runs

architecture_history: original hypothesis (unverified): CAGRA wins as historical index scales to 10k-100k+ points
measured finding: CAGRA never wins at query batch_size=1, regardless of index size up to 500,000 points; brute_force always wins at batch=1
measured finding: CAGRA wins decisively at query batch_size>=1000 (background/batch workloads)

architectural redesign: hot path no longer searches the full historical index at all; background GPU refit (HDBSCAN via cuML, at batch sizes where CAGRA is measured to win) periodically compresses the historical attractor map into ~50-100 centroids with per-centroid anomaly radii (epsilon)
hot path now performs O(K) centroid lookup (K=100) via AVX2 instead of O(N) or O(log N) search against the full historical index
measured result: centroid lookup at K=100 costs 0.233us mean, beating the lead's <0.5us target by more than 2x
fused end-to-end hot-path measurement (Layer 1 + Layer 2 in one measured call): 1.81us mean, 3.25us p99, 6.72us p999
not_yet_done: no CPU pinning or real-time kernel tuning applied to any measurement in this report; p999 of 6.72us (roughly 3.7x the mean) is consistent with unpinned OS scheduler jitter and should improve substantially with CPU affinity and a real-time-patched kernel

the background GPU refit path that produces the centroid+epsilon map has not yet been implemented in C++, nor has the shadow-swap (double-buffered atomic pointer) mechanism connecting it to the hot-path consumer described in the lead's Task 3

argmin over K=100 centroids uses a scalar loop, not vectorized reduction; not yet benchmarked against an AVX2 horizontal-reduction alternative, though the current cost (0.23us) is already well within target
Layer 0 (ingest, adjacency matrix construction) and Layer 4 (decision table lookup) have not been included in this fused measurement; this is Layer 1+2 only
